- **Bounded body recheck after a body-only round.** When a remediation round edits only the PR body, the harness first asks whether the prior review's findings were all PR-body findings. `fidelity.body_recheck` reads the prior verdict file and `fidelity.body_recheck_eligibility` (through `body_only_findings_text`) returns the bullets only when the failing-check set is exactly check 4 (4a, 4b and 4c count as 4), every `## FINDINGS` bullet carries a `[BLOCKING]` or `[NOTE]` marker, no bullet cites another check, and `REVIEW-COVERAGE` is `CURRENT` or absent. An unrecognised layout returns `None`. `fidelity.body_recheck` then requires the head tree to equal that file's `REVIEWED_TREE=` line and the plan hash to be unchanged, numbers the prior findings `F1..Fn` and the added or changed body hunks `H1..Hm` (`llm_calls.body_hunks`, a line diff of the body the prior review read against the new one), and runs one single-turn Sonnet call with the diff sections the findings and hunks name as evidence. `schemas.validate_body_recheck` demands every id exactly once with a closed status enum. The round passes only when every finding is `resolved` and every hunk is `supported`; it then writes a `READY` verdict file at the re-review path with the prior digest carried forward and `REVIEWED_TREE=` recorded, so `select_fidelity_verdict` and arming condition (12) read it exactly as they read a re-review. Every other outcome (ineligible, invalid output, a `HarnessError`, an `unresolved` finding, an `unsupported` hunk) falls through to the unchanged full Opus re-review. The recheck never writes `NOT READY`. `result.json` records `rounds[].review_kind` (`body-recheck` or `full`) and `rounds[].recheck_fallback_reason`. `bench/replay_body_only_recheck.py` replays the predicate over `out/live-*` and, with `--live`, the real call.
- **One fix round before the sticky verdict.** When the first arming evaluation holds on condition (2), (3) or (11), `harness/fix_round.py` runs one bounded round before anything is recorded or posted. It reuses `thread_ingestion.disposition_thread` for review threads and unthreaded findings, and `conformance_fix.remediate_missing` for MISSING items. Both defer: no reply and no push happen inside the round. The round gets at most 8 items and 1200 seconds. A delta review and the conformance check then judge the new head. A new holding finding, a worse conformance result, a degraded review, a timeout or an error discards the round with `git.drop_commit`, so the original hold stands. An accepted round is pushed, the deferred replies are posted, and the unchanged `_evaluate_arm` re-reads every arming input on the new head. One round per run. `holdrepeat` keeps a per-branch `fix_round` record capped at 3 attempts and skips a repeat on the same holds. `POSTPLAN_FIX_ROUND=0` turns it off; `bin/post-plan-now` passes the value through. The record is `fix-round.json` in the run dir and `result.json` `fix_round`; the sticky carries one `Fix round:` line.
- **Phase 7 byte-budget carve-out (ADR-0184).** When the triaged failing checks are exactly `Static guards` and `bin/check-rules-byte-budget` fails in the worktree before the fix, `_ci_fix_loop` tells the ci-fix fixer which `.claude/rules/*.md` files already in the PR diff it may shrink, and allows one new `*-detail.md` companion with a `paths:` list. `harness/rules_budget_carveout.py` re-checks the commit with git: each modified rules file must be smaller than before, each added one must be a companion with `paths:`, and any other gate-owning path, deletion or rename refuses the whole commit. It then reruns `bin/check-rules-byte-budget`, `bin/check-prose --since=origin/master` and `bin/check-docs --since=origin/master --no-staleness`. A refusal takes the existing `error:gate-path-edit` exit. Thread ingestion and prosefix keep the full deny; the Phase 5.5 fixer has its own, separate carve-out below.
- **Phase 4.5 unreachable-defect filing.** A fixer that declines a thread as `not-worth-it` may add a `followup` key (title, harm, trigger) when the defect is real and its fix needs a file it may not edit. `thread_ingestion.file_declined_followup` files it as a `maintenance` backlog issue through the per-PR follow-up cap, after the thread resolves. Only the harms `crash`, `wrong-value`, `lost-data` and `security` file. A malformed key files nothing, a title already filed under `maintenance` files nothing, matched on its first 60 normalised characters, and a filing failure is a log line. In a fix round the filing waits for `fix_round.flush`, so a discarded round files nothing.
- **Phase 4.5 outdated threads.** `_run_thread_ingestion_phase` calls `run_thread_ingestion` with `include_outdated=True`, so `list_trusted_open_threads <PR> --include-outdated` also returns trusted threads whose diff hunk is gone (`isOutdated`, `line` null). Earlier runs left those open for good: the shell default and `fetch_trusted_threads` both dropped them while `pr_unresolved_findings_hold` kept counting them, so arming condition (11) never cleared. The fixer gets no file excerpt for such a thread; the prompt says the anchor is gone, tells it to open the path on the current tree and search for what the finding names, and names DECLINE `already-fixed` as the expected verdict when the tree already addresses it. At most `MAX_OUTDATED_PER_PASS` (12) outdated threads run per pass, oldest `commentId` first; current threads are never capped. The rest stay open, keep holding (11), and are counted as `deferred_outdated` in `thread-ingestion.json` next to `outdated_found` and a per-thread `outdated` flag. A run of outdated threads the fixer keeps skipping can sit at the head of that cap and starve newer ones; the count makes it visible. Human-authored threads, labelled Nit and Pre-existing threads, gate-held threads and the fail-closed `None` on a `gh` failure are unchanged. Phase 4.5b and the skill fallback keep the live-hunk rule.
- **Phase 4.5b same-run thread remediation.** After the review worker is joined, the harness takes a second `pr_thread_ids` snapshot. Ids absent from the pre-posting snapshot whose `(path, body prefix)` match a finding this process posted through `post_review_findings` are this run's own threads. They go through the same Phase 4.5 fixer, packet, trust contract and commit/push/resolve path (`harness/same_run_threads.py`), once. A fix commit re-keys the Phase 7 CI watch to the new head, re-runs Phase 5.0 conformance, re-pins fidelity verdict 2 when one exists, and triggers one review of the fix delta only; new findings from it are posted and left open. Fixed or declined findings leave the in-memory list arming condition (2) reads. Any thread the fixer skips, and any thread not posted by this process, still holds under condition (11). `result.json` records the pass under `thread_ingestion.same_run` only when it found candidates.
- **Phase 5.0-pre conformance fixer.** After Phase 4.5 and before the review worker starts, the harness runs the conformance check once without a Phase 5 status and hands the fixable items (`MISSING-METHOD:`, a test-path `MISSING:`, a non-denied `MISSING-FILE:`, `UNREALISED-ASSERTION:`) to one Sonnet round in `harness/conformance_fix.py`. `MISSING-PHASE:` and `UNMET-CONTRACT:` never reach it. The round has no Bash and runs with the gate-fix tool lists. It is skipped on a dirty tree or more than 6 fixable items. Its edits are reverted when it writes outside the plan-cited paths, touches a gate-owning path, removes or changes an existing line, passes the line caps, writes a test with a skip marker or no assertion, or leaves a promised method unwritten. A crash also reverts the tree. What survives is committed and pushed through the gate-fix wrappers, and the tree is refreshed so Phase 5 verify runs the new tests. This pass writes no `conformance-done` marker. Condition (3) is decided by the final Phase 5.0 pass alone, and its hold detail ends with `[conformance-fix: <reason>]`. `result.json` records the round under `conformance_fix`. `POSTPLAN_CONFORMANCE_FIX=0` disables it (ADR-0216).
- **Phase 5.5 file-fix carve-out (ADR-0204).** Before the remediation fixer spawns, `harness/fidelity_filefix.py` reads the `[BLOCKING]` bullets under the verdict's `## FINDINGS` heading and collects every `.claude/rules/*.md` file they name in a code span (full path, or a basename unique among the PR's changed files) that the PR diff against `origin/master` already touches. `fidelity.remediate` tells the fixer that set. After the commit it re-checks with git: each gate-owning hit must be in the set, be a modification, change at most 20 lines with at most 8 deletions, and keep its frontmatter identical apart from `last_verified`; at most 3 files and 40 lines in total. It then reruns `bin/check-rules-byte-budget`, `bin/check-prose --since=origin/master` and `bin/check-docs --since=origin/master --no-staleness`. Any refusal takes the existing `gate-path-edit` exit with the commit left local. Workflows, `bin/check-*`, `harness/armable.py` and the rest of `LOCAL_GATE_PATH_PREFIXES` never enter the set. The run log records the snapshot as `file-fix carve-out active for <files>` or `inactive (<reason>)`.
